findings.body:
**Authorization middleware removed from admin endpoints.**

Previously both handlers were wrapped with `middleware.RequireRole("admin")`. This diff registers bare `http.HandlerFunc(a.listUsers)` / `a.editRoles` on the v2 subrouter, so the admin role check no longer runs at the routing layer.

**Failure mode:** any authenticated or unauthenticated caller who can hit `GET /api/v2/admin/users` or `POST /api/v2/admin/roles` can list users and modify roles, depending on what (if anything) the handlers enforce internally.

**Fix:** restore the middleware on the new routes:

```suggestion
        v2.Handle("/admin/users", authz(http.HandlerFunc(a.listUsers))).Methods("GET")
```

(and the same `authz(...)` wrap on `/admin/roles`), keeping `authz := middleware.RequireRole("admin")` above the subrouter registrations. Alternatively, attach `authz` via `v2.Use(...)` if the subrouter is admin-only.

**Same authz drop on the role-edit endpoint.**

`POST /api/v2/admin/roles` is now registered without `RequireRole("admin")`. This is a privilege-escalation / unauthorized-write surface: clients can change roles without passing the admin gate that existed on `/admin/roles`.

Restore the wrapper:

```suggestion
        v2.Handle("/admin/roles", authz(http.HandlerFunc(a.editRoles))).Methods("POST")
```

with `authz := middleware.RequireRole("admin")` still defined in `routes`.

**Old `/admin/*` routes are removed with no compatibility path.**

Clients still calling `GET /admin/users` or `POST /admin/roles` will get 404 after this ships. If the versioning rollout is intentional, add a short-term redirect or dual-register the old paths (still behind `RequireRole("admin")`) until consumers move to `/api/v2/admin/...`, or call out the break in a major-version release note.

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this change removes admin role authorization from privileged endpoints while relocating them under `/api/v2`.

## Findings

| # | Severity | File | Summary |
|---|----------|------|---------|
| 1 | 🚨 critical | `cmd/server/routes.go:6` | `RequireRole("admin")` wrapper removed from both admin handlers |
| 2 | ⚠️ warning  | `cmd/server/routes.go:5` | Old `/admin/*` paths dropped with no redirect or compatibility layer |

## Details

The diff replaces:

```go
authz := middleware.RequireRole("admin")
r.Handle("/admin/users", authz(http.HandlerFunc(a.listUsers))).Methods("GET")
r.Handle("/admin/roles", authz(http.HandlerFunc(a.editRoles))).Methods("POST")
```

with unauthenticated registrations on a `/api/v2` subrouter. Unless equivalent auth is applied inside `listUsers` / `editRoles` or on a parent router (neither is visible in this change), any caller who can reach the process can list users and edit roles.

The path move itself is consistent with the stated versioning work, but deleting the old routes without a deprecation/redirect path will break existing admin clients on `/admin/users` and `/admin/roles`.

## Release decision

**Recommendation:** request-changes
